Notes

Old internet swagger meets half a yuan, a potholed road and anxiety about being used. The voice claims to be a legend while asking to be left out of the record.

哥

哥, gē, is literally older brother, but as a self-reference it claims a relaxed seniority: “your boy,” with the implication that this speaker deserves recognition. It is different from the harsher 老子 later in the verse. The song can shift from teasing internet swagger to aggression simply by changing what the speaker calls himself.

  • Genius community transcript
只是个传说

The longer slogan “don’t be obsessed with me; I’m only a legend” was already cataloged among 2009 internet catchphrases in a study hosted by East China Normal University. This line carries that recognizable boast, while the next asks to be treated as if the speaker never appeared. Legend and disappearance sit side by side.

  • East China Normal University-hosted study, table of 2009 internet catchphrases
  • Lyric text
就当我从没来过

The claim to legendary status is paired with a request for erasure. That combination lets the speaker enjoy recognition while refusing ordinary access to himself. Later, he explains why he cannot tell much of his story: others could use it. The hook’s disappearance is therefore more pointed than simple modesty after a boast.

  • Lyric transcript
实的

实 contrasts with the previous line’s 虚: solid or real versus hollow, shaky, or lacking confidence. The opposition works through both the body and credibility. A few lines later, having only half a yuan still does not prevent the speaker from carrying himself with style.

  • Lyric text
常走在河边脚都不湿的

The familiar warning asks how anyone can keep walking by a river without getting their shoes wet: repeated exposure to trouble eventually catches up with you. This line grants the speaker exactly that impossible exemption. The boast is not that he avoids risky ground, but that the usual consequences fail to stick to him.

  • Genius community transcript
五毛钱

五毛 is fifty fen, half of one yuan: deliberately little pocket money. The next line insists that style survives that lack. Coming after claims to surpass everyone combined, this is an anti-flex inside the flex: the speaker makes charisma independent of expensive proof, just as “Poker Face” puts dignity before earnings.

  • Lyric transcript
咋个管

咋个 is a colloquial, regionally marked way of asking “how.” 管 can mean manage, control, or interfere with someone. Here the whole question challenges the other people’s ability to police his behavior, rather than asking them for practical guidance.

  • Lyric text
淘汰

淘汰 is being eliminated, selected out or rendered obsolete. It makes the rivalry sound like a competitive process with losers who stop counting. The response is helpless anger at empty air, while the speaker watches from the side. His superiority is performed as freedom from the very contest that has made the others frantic.

  • Lyric transcript
吃着瓜

吃瓜, chī guā, literally means eating melon; online it describes watching other people’s drama as a spectator. The preceding 看戏, watching a show, gives the same stance in an older image. Together they make detachment pleasurable: while the other person rages at thin air, the speaker settles in to enjoy the performance.

  • Genius community transcript
利用我

利用 means putting something to use and, with a person as object, taking advantage of them. The danger arrives at the point of greatest visibility, not at failure. That interrupts the earlier carefree cool: becoming more successful also makes one’s story useful material for others, giving the refusal to disclose it a protective purpose.

  • Lyric transcript
小卡拉米

小卡拉米, xiǎo kǎlāmi, dismisses someone as an insignificant little character, roughly “small fry.” Its comic sound cuts the threatening social pose down to size before 社会, street toughness, inflates it again. Repeating the pairing lets the little nobody and the big pose keep colliding in the same breath.

  • Lyric transcript
社会很社会

社会 ordinarily means society, but as a colloquial adjective it can praise or mock streetwise toughness. 社会很社会 uses the word in both positions, making the explanation deliberately circular: society is very “society.” Following the repeated dismissal of petty nobodies, the tautology mocks a scene whose claim to depth may consist mainly of its own tough label.

  • Genius community transcript
坑坑洼洼的土路

坑坑洼洼 doubles pits and hollows into a bumpy four-syllable texture. After the repeated grand word “society,” the verse gives us a road that still cannot be repaired properly. The mundane failure punctures the surrounding performance of power: all that talk of being streetwise has not made the actual ground easier to travel.

  • Lyric transcript
时间会知道的

Time is personified as the eventual witness. After restricting access to his story and asserting that he is real, the speaker postpones judgment to something less manipulable than the current crowd. The phrase promises vindication without supplying it now, before the hook returns to the paradox of becoming a legend and disappearing.

  • Lyric transcript

About Jackzebra and this mixtape

Zhuang Zhuang Mixtape arrived on Surf Gang on October 2, 2026: 55 tracks, opening with Sour and closing with Sweet. Its cast widens from YoungQueenz on Poker Face to User116, Effie, kuru, yoyi, 春 and 南部犯罪份子. Aghast has a production credit on every track from Hitman through Snatch, giving that stretch a shared collaborator behind its changing scenes.

Surf Gang release · Artist credits

Jackzebra told AVYSS that he writes while singing over a beat he has listened to repeatedly, keeping the images in his head central. He values the room Mandarin leaves for indirect meanings. Listen for ordinary phrases becoming physical scenes: familiarity becomes cooking, authority becomes family seniority, and a tired saying suddenly turns into a threat.

AVYSS interview, 2024

In STATIC, he describes mixtapes as a format for letting ideas flow, reserving an official debut album for later. In a separate conversation about Above & Beyond, he compared that earlier tape to a collection of his producer friends’ work. The credits here likewise reward attention: long-running collaborators sit alongside guests working in Mandarin, Korean and English.

STATIC interview · Sabukaru interview, 2025

The small details connect to his stated interests: he has described playing Temple Run in transit and before shows, watching Top Boy, and wanting to score White Oleander. These give the songs specific points of contact with his life. The notes follow those connections alongside the lyrics’ jokes, invented scenes and competing voices.

His recommendations in Perfectly Imperfect · Dazed interview, 2025 · Interview questionnaire, 2025

Jackzebra has pushed back on being made to represent all of China’s underground. These notes stay close to the words: what an expression usually means, what changes in this line, and how another song answers it. Cultural references have sources; interpretations rest on details you can hear or read in the song.
